- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.8) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3–5% above recent peak unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.2) and prices are trending up, model underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to account for mean reversion bias.
- When sentiment swings from positive to negative, model lags in adjusting; delay forecast correction by 1–2 periods unless sentiment confirms reversal.
- For 30-day horizon, model consistently overestimates in early periods (first 5–7 days) when sentiment is neutral or slightly positive; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% for first 5 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “0.00” or “negative” values, model underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to compensate for low sentiment bias.
- When sentiment is high and price is near historical mean, model tends to overcorrect; reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought conditions.
